figures.caption: Figure 1: REALM augments language model pre-training with a neural knowledge retriever that retrieves knowledge from a textual knowledge corpus , 𝒵 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} (e.g., all of Wikipedia). Signal from the language modeling objective backpropagates all the way through the retriever, which must consider millions of documents in 𝒵 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} —a significant computational challenge that we address.

Figure 2: The overall framework of REALM. Left: Unsupervised pre-training. The knowledge retriever and knowledge-augmented encoder are jointly pre-trained on the unsupervised language modeling task. Right: Supervised fine-tuning. After the parameters of the retriever ( θ 𝜃 \theta ) and encoder ( ϕ italic-ϕ \phi ) have been pre-trained, they are then fine-tuned on a task of primary interest, using supervised examples.
Figure 3: REALM pre-training with asynchronous MIPS refreshes.
